🇮🇳❤🇧🇩 **Beautiful Bangladesh, Beautiful People!**

Being an Indian living very close to Bangladesh, I have had the pleasure of visiting this beautiful country several times. Every visit has left me with wonderful memories. The lush green landscapes, peaceful rivers, vibrant markets, delicious traditional food, colourful festivals, and, above all, the warmth, simplicity, and hospitality of the Bangladeshi people have truly touched my heart.

I especially admire the rich Bengali culture, mouth-watering fish dishes, biryani, sweets, and the festive spirit of Pohela Boishakh and Eid.

Although we belong to two different nations, our shared language, culture, traditions, and emotions create a beautiful bond.

**Borders may divide countries, but hearts, culture, and humanity bring people together.**

Lots of love and respect from an Indian neighbour! 🇮🇳🤝🇧🇩❤

comments.author: @piranhagobler8432
comments.text: Population explosion is a huge factor in the dire economic situation Bangladesh is in. Unless the people and the government take measures to control the population the people will continue to suffer economically and socially. Contraception is a must if Bangladeshis wish to improve their living conditions.

replies.author: @piranhagobler8432
replies.text: @UnseenPlanettFewer children in a family means more financial resources to go around for the welfare of the entire family.

replies.author: @UnseenPlanett
replies.text: If two working parents in Bangladesh can barely afford to raise one child, why do we question their family size before we question their pay?

replies.author: @UnseenPlanett
replies.text: People should be free to decide whether and when to have children, with access to contraception if they want it. Wages and rent also shape what a family can afford each month.

replies.author: @piranhagobler8432
replies.text: @UnseenWorldDocs_UsFamily planning would put an end to explosive population growth within months. Other measures take time and money. The latter is in very short supply in Bangladesh and likely to be so for a long time. Family planning is the first and most important step now which will prevent further deterioration in poverty, exploitation of children and women and help the government to improve the living standards of the population.

replies.author: @UnseenWorldDocs_Us
replies.text: Population pressure can definitely make housing, jobs, education, and public services harder to manage, but it’s probably only one part of the picture. What do you think Bangladesh should prioritize first—family planning, job creation, or infrastructure?
